title: Blackjack
subtitle: Monte Carlo Exploring Starts
overview: A classic card game where the goal is to beat the dealer by getting a hand value as close to 21 as possible without going over.
rules: Cards 2-10 are worth their face value
Face cards (J, Q, K) are worth 10
Aces are worth 1 or 11 (whichever is better)
Dealer must hit on 16, stand on 17

algorithm.name: Monte Carlo Exploring Starts
algorithm.description: The AI learns optimal play by simulating hundreds of thousands of games and tracking which actions lead to wins in each situation.

proof.explanation: The state space is derived from all possible combinations of game variables that affect decision-making.
proof.formula: |S| = (Player totals) x (Dealer cards) x (Usable ace) = 10 x 10 x 2 = 200
steps: Player total: 12-21 (10 values) - below 12, always hit
Dealer showing: 2-11 (10 values) - Ace counted as 11
proof.conclusion: Each of these 200 states requires learning the optimal action (hit or stand).

proof.explanation: The house edge represents the casino's expected profit per bet.
proof.formula: House Edge = P(player busts first) + P(dealer wins | no bust) - P(player wins) ≈ 0.5%
steps: Player must act first - if they bust, they lose regardless
This 'first-mover disadvantage' is the primary source
Net effect with optimal play: ~0.5% house advantage
proof.conclusion: Even with perfect play, the house maintains a 0.5% edge.

proof.explanation: Monte Carlo methods require sufficient visits to each state-action pair to converge.
proof.formula: Required: Each (s,a) visited ~1000+ times. 400 pairs x 1000 = 400,000+ episodes
steps: Each pair needs ~1000 samples for stable estimates
proof.conclusion: After 500,000 episodes, Q-values converge to optimal with high confidence.

keyInsight: The learned policy matches the mathematically proven optimal basic strategy.
